title: Legacy CPAT bugs and the CPAT-AI register v8.4 (workbook v8.4)

definitions.definition: Legacy bug: legacy CPAT does not compute what it means to (a wrong row, a double application, a dead reference); the fix is a change of formulas.
Data bug: a problem in the input data that the prototype does not replicate (it fills or corrects the data); the fix is a change of the input data, and each data bug has a plan.
definitions.prototype: Departs until the data are fixed; then reads the data as legacy.

definitions.definition: Prototype bug: a defect of the prototype itself, found and fixed during development.
Issue: legacy does what it means to, but the choice is open to question (a method, a default, a convention), or a limitation of the prototype.
definitions.prototype: Replicates it and tracks it; a departure only by user decision, recorded with the issue.

definitions.definition: Data issue: an issue of the input data (vintage, gaps, conventions) that the prototype replicates: it does what legacy does with the data as they are.
Departure: a row of the prototype's LegacyDiff sheet that is not "Same" (a decision, a simplification, a part not built yet).
Upgrade: a possible improvement beyond legacy.

other_mitigation_areas.about: Population, GDP growth and the GDP-effect multipliers: everything downstream depends on them.
Price parameters, pass-through, VAT, consumer and producer subsidies, and the average-price reports.
Methane, flaring, waste and the local-pollutant emission factors and totals.
Regulation shares and adjustments, feebate inclusion and rates.
New and existing ETS, existing carbon taxes, coverage and the shadow prices.
Sector fuel-use blocks (aviation, other energy use, residential, road), exemptions and leakage, manual power investment.
Energy trade balance and current account.
Revenue rows and the revenue reports.
Manual-input blocks and the names that read them.

records.title: GDP effect added to GDP growth every year
